question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -4}\frac{3x+12}{{x}^{3}+64} & =\frac{3(-4)+12}{(-4)^{3}+64}=\frac{-12+12}{-64+64}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. 

Notice that the denominator is a sum of cubes. Therefore, factoring our expression, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3x+12}{{x}^{3}+64} & =\frac{3(x+4)}{{x}^{3}+{4}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{3(x+4)}{(x+4)({x}^{2}-4x+{4}^{2})} \\  & =\frac{3}{{x}^{2}-4x+16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -4}\frac{3x+12}{{x}^{3}+64} & ={lim}_{x\to -4}\frac{3}{{x}^{2}-4x+16} \\  & =\frac{3}{(-4)^{2}-4(-4)+16} \\  & =\frac{3}{16+16+16} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$
